options.counterfactual: Every compact set that is the closure of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain in complex Euclidean space has an Oka complement, even without a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Investigate a complement theorem based on local polynomial convexity rather than global polynomial convexity. Determine whether its precise hypotheses cover all the compact domains in the definition of S.

options.counterfactual: Every compact set that is the closure of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain in complex Euclidean space has an Oka complement, even without a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Investigate whether Oka approximation can be propagated inward from the exterior of a large ball across a pseudoconcave collar. Focus on how weak Levi degeneracy could be handled without assuming Stein neighbourhoods of the obstacle.

options.counterfactual: Every compact set that is the closure of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain in complex Euclidean space has an Oka complement, even without a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Examine whether pseudoconvex domains admit interior exhaustions whose Oka complements provide quantitatively controlled entire approximants. Identify the additional compactness or avoidance estimates needed to pass to the limiting exterior.

options.counterfactual: An Oka complement of a smoothly bounded compact domain forces that compact domain to have a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Seek a precise statement and proof of this necessary-condition theorem, checking carefully that it concerns Oka complements rather than elliptic complements or a stronger approximation property. If verified, combine it with worm domains and the local Hartogs obstruction to determine both dimension sets.

options.counterfactual: An Oka complement of a smoothly bounded compact domain forces that compact domain to have a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Try to derive Stein neighbourhoods directly from convex approximation by constructing holomorphic separators between the compact obstacle and exterior points. Identify whether the construction actually gives neighbourhood separation rather than only entire curves through exterior points.

options.counterfactual: An Oka complement of a smoothly bounded compact domain forces that compact domain to have a Stein neighbourhood basis.
options.approach: Investigate a weaker necessary hull property sufficient to exclude worm domains and negative tangential Levi directions. This could determine the dimension sets without proving the full Stein-neighbourhood assertion.

options.counterfactual: For every n at least three, the exterior of the compact domain defined by ||z'||² + (|w|² − 1)² ≤ 4 is Oka, despite its nonpseudoconvex boundary.
options.approach: Investigate a parameter-dependent compact-complement theorem for the projection onto w, whose nonempty obstacle fibers are convex balls. Check explicitly whether the theorem permits fibers to disappear and their complements to change topology.

options.counterfactual: For every n at least three, the exterior of the compact domain defined by ||z'||² + (|w|² − 1)² ≤ 4 is Oka, despite its nonpseudoconvex boundary.
options.approach: Attempt to construct dominating holomorphic sprays along arbitrary maps from neighbourhoods of compact convex sets into this exterior. Use the extra horizontal coordinate available when n is at least three, and address holomorphic dependence rather than merely pointwise entire curves.

options.counterfactual: For every n at least three, the exterior of the compact domain defined by ||z'||² + (|w|² − 1)² ≤ 4 is Oka, despite its nonpseudoconvex boundary.
options.approach: Seek a Zariski-open Oka covering of the exterior by placing portions of the obstacle in Stein ambient manifolds with the density property. Verify both holomorphic convexity of the relevant compact obstacles and coverage of points near the mixed-Levi boundary.
